title: The Last Rounder after-hours spot
summary: The Last Rounder was the last place to go and the last band to knock off, still playing at nine in the morning. Ernie played there with King Jimmy Davis and others.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: All night long, 4, 5 o'clock in the morning. Now they had another place right there where, where you got this little restaurant there on the corner from Pellano, what you call it, Virginia Kitchen? Yeah, yeah. Every place they used to call the Last Rounder.
Yeah, next year's what they did.

You could pass there at 9 o'clock in the morning and still hear the band playing from the night before. That was the last rounder. That was the last band that would knock off. Everybody knocked off their still playing. The Last Rounders, the last place you could go to see the new music. Who played there? Oh, I played there several times. Yeah, I was playing there a little bit. Yeah. King Jimmy Davis, we stood there a good while with the two twins. Yeah, the trumpet player with twins. Yeah. And the drummer himself. About five pieces. I played there with Kid Harris. Kid Harvey played there. Most of us played there.
Big band banjo, little short dance.
